title: File federal payroll taxes (Form 941)
summary: Employers report wages, tips, federal income tax withheld, and Social Security and Medicare taxes on Form 941 each quarter, due the last day of the month after the quarter. Very small employers (employment tax of $1,000 a year or less) may be allowed to file Form 944 once a year instead.
action: File Form 941 each quarter and deposit payroll taxes on time. If all taxes were deposited on time, you get 10 extra days to file.
verify: last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter

title: File federal unemployment tax (Form 940)
summary: Most employers file Form 940 once a year to report federal unemployment (FUTA) tax, due January 31. Paying Maryland unemployment tax on time gets you the most credit against FUTA.
action: File Form 940 by January 31. If you deposited all FUTA tax on time, you have 10 extra days.

title: Send W-2s to Social Security
summary: By January 31, file Forms W-2 with Form W-3 with the Social Security Administration and give each employee their W-2. Employers filing 10 or more information returns in total must file electronically.
action: File W-2s through SSA Business Services Online and give copies to employees by January 31.
verify: Forms W-2 are required to be provided to employees by Jan. 31

title: Send 1099s to contractors you paid
summary: If you paid independent contractors (non-employees) for services above the IRS reporting threshold, you must file Form 1099-NEC with the IRS and send a copy to each contractor by January 31.
action: Collect a W-9 from each contractor during the year. By January 31, file 1099-NECs (online through IRIS) and send copies to contractors. Check the IRS instructions for the current dollar threshold.
verify: file Form 1099-NEC on or before January 31

title: Federal ownership report (BOI): no longer required
summary: Companies formed in the United States no longer have to file beneficial ownership (BOI) reports with FinCEN. FinCEN made this exemption permanent in a final rule in August 2026. Rules could change again.
action: Nothing to file if your company was formed in the U.S.
verify: U.S. companies are exempt from BOI reporting requirements

title: Get a federal Employer Identification Number (EIN)
summary: You generally need an EIN from the IRS to hire employees or to run a partnership or corporation. Form your LLC or corporation with the state first, then apply. An EIN is free from the IRS.
action: Apply for an EIN directly on IRS.gov. Never pay a website to get one.
verify: You never have to pay a fee for an EIN
sourceName: IRS: Get an employer identification number

title: Complete Form I-9 for every new hire
summary: Every U.S. employer must fill out Form I-9 with each person it hires, including U.S. citizens, to check identity and permission to work. Keep each form for 3 years after the hire date or 1 year after the job ends, whichever is later.
action: Complete Form I-9 with each new hire and keep the forms on file, ready for inspection.
verify: for three years after the date of hire
sourceName: USCIS: Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification

title: Put up the federal workplace posters that apply to you
summary: Several federal labor laws require notices to be posted where employees can see them. Which posters you need depends on which laws cover your business.
action: Use the U.S. Department of Labor's poster page to find and print the posters that apply to you, free.
verify: require that notices be provided to employees and/or posted in the workplace
sourceName: U.S. Department of Labor: Workplace posters

title: File the yearly EEO-1 workforce report
summary: Private employers with 100 or more employees must send workforce data (job category, sex, race or ethnicity) to the EEOC each year. Some federal contractors with 50 or more employees must file too.
action: Watch the EEOC's EEO-1 page for when the yearly collection opens, then file by its deadline.
frequencyNote: When the EEOC opens the yearly collection
verify: private sector employers with 100 or more employees
federal contractors with 50 or more employees

title: Register in SAM.gov to bid on federal contracts
summary: To bid on federal contracts or apply for federal awards directly, you need an active SAM.gov registration, which gives you a Unique Entity ID. You don't need one if you only sell to state or local agencies.
action: If you sell to federal agencies, register at SAM.gov and renew every 365 days.
verify: You must renew your registration every 365 days
